summary:
COSMOCare is an intelligent astronaut health-monitoring and risk-assessment platform designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. It provides a centralized system for monitoring astronaut health indicators, reviewing mission alerts, exploring risk-assessment information and understanding potential health concerns.

The platform combines a health-monitoring dashboard, backend services, machine learning capabilities, simulation tools and an AI-powered chatbot. It enables users to explore astronaut profiles, review biometric indicators, examine health notifications and interact with COSMOCare Assistant for mission-related health information.

By bringing health monitoring, data analysis and conversational assistance into one platform, COSMOCare aims to support better-informed health-management decisions and contribute to safer future human space exploration.
details:
COSMOCare – Astronaut Health Monitoring & Risk Assessment System

1. Introduction

COSMOCare is an astronaut health-monitoring and risk-assessment platform developed to address the challenges of maintaining astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. Spaceflight introduces health challenges such as radiation exposure, microgravity-related physiological changes and the need for continuous monitoring of vital indicators.

COSMOCare aims to bring health information, mission notifications and analytical tools together in one centralized platform.

2. How COSMOCare Works

COSMOCare provides several integrated modules:

  • Mission Dashboard: Provides an overview of mission operations, crew statistics, monitoring status and recent alerts.
  • Astronaut Directory: Maintains astronaut profiles, crew identification and individual monitoring information.
  • Health Monitoring: Displays available biometric indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen, sleep duration, temperature and radiation-related information.
  • Risk Assessment: Presents astronaut risk indicators, assessment summaries and illustrative risk information.
  • Alert Management: Organizes health notifications according to severity and status.
  • Mission Timeline: Provides a chronological overview of mission activities and health-monitoring events.
  • Simulation: Allows users to adjust hypothetical health parameters and explore illustrative scenario outcomes.
  • COSMOCare AI Assistant: Provides conversational assistance for understanding astronaut health indicators, mission information, alerts and risk-assessment concepts.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

COSMOCare aims to support astronaut health management by centralizing available health information and presenting potential concerns in an understandable format.

Its intended benefits include improved visibility of astronaut health information, easier review of health notifications, accessible explanations of health-monitoring concepts and support for informed mission-health management.

4. Technologies Used

COSMOCare follows a modular software architecture integrating frontend development, backend services, machine learning and conversational AI.

The implementation uses the technologies and libraries documented in the project repository, including:

  • Frontend development framework and libraries.
  • Python-based backend services and APIs.
  • Machine learning components.
  • AI-powered chatbot technology.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration.

5. Creativity and Innovation

COSMOCare combines astronaut health monitoring, risk-assessment interfaces, mission alerts, simulation and conversational AI in one integrated platform.

Its modular approach provides a foundation for connecting astronaut health information with analytical and decision-support capabilities for future space exploration.

6. Future Scope

Future improvements include real-time wearable sensor integration, expanded NASA space-health dataset integration, more advanced predictive models, personalized astronaut health profiles and enhanced autonomous decision-support capabilities.

COSMOCare is a research prototype and decision-support platform, not a clinically validated medical diagnostic system.
